summary: The Chief has a strong ceremonial silhouette, but the everyday characters still read as modern shirts and trousers with pale apron panels. The caravan leader needs a much clearer mammoth-herder identity. Stone Age materials, everyday silhouette separation and attachment quality need another pass.
problems: Red/green shirt shapes, straight blue/tan trousers and regular boot bands dominate the everyday kits. Small hide patches do not overcome the modern-clothing read.
Flintworker and Scout have almost identical torso silhouettes; their handheld tools do most of the differentiation. Hearthkeeper is also too close to this same template.
Gatherer's grass construction is not apparent in this view. The smooth cylindrical container reads as a manufactured pail rather than a woven gathering basket.
The caravan leader's square blue case resembles modern luggage. The hood and three small shells suggest a generic traveller, not an unmistakable visiting mammoth herder.
The Chief's antlers and skull staff successfully signal authority, but the mantle reads as rectangular boards rather than a substantial animal pelt.

Basket and luggage grips are not visibly continuous with their containers. Several tools sit alongside the arms without a convincing hand grip; broad shoulder pieces also need clearance checks during animation.
Tiny ties, pins, facial paint and bag markings cannot carry identity at stream scale. The supplied near-frontal view does not establish readability from the game's elevated camera.
fix: All kits: replace the exposed modern shirt/trouser treatment with visibly constructed hide, fur or plant-fibre garments. Hide default sleeves where they remain visible; use skin-matched bare limbs or individually fitted hide leggings, not recoloured jeans. Keep rigid lower panels clear of moving legs. Flintworker of the Sinew Seam: make the hide wrap distinctly one-shouldered with a stepped, uneven hem; enlarge the flint head and its binding into one readable tool silhouette, seat the shaft through the hand, and retain the asymmetric calf wraps. Overlapping-Grass Gatherer: bring the layered grass mantle over the shoulders so its stepped fringe is visible from above; replace the smooth pail with a squat basket using a few broad woven bands and a continuous handle attached at both sides. Hearthkeeper in the Folded Shoulder Hide: remove the visible default sleeves, enlarge the folded hide into a single thick asymmetric shoulder drape, and give the lower wrap a longer, clearly different outline; keep the pin seated against the fold and the staff gripped. Young Ridge Scout: shorten the hide wrap, expose more limb or use minimal fitted wraps, remove the apron-like front rectangle, and strengthen the stone spearhead and binding; keep this the lightest, narrowest silhouette. Chief of the Great Branched Antlers: preserve the antlers and skull staff, reshape the slab collar into overlapping pelt lobes with a chunky irregular edge, and anchor every antler branch visibly into the hide headpiece. Far-Roving Shell-Cowl Mammoth Herder: replace the case with a rounded hide pack on a connected strap, broaden the fur cowl, and add a large ivory tusk toggle or paired tusk ornaments visible from above; retain shells as secondary regional decoration. Re-render both body variants at the actual 40-degree town camera and thumbnail scale, including an arm-swing pose to check grips, shoulders and leg clearance.
